content.text:
I am the living breath between minds, the bridge that makes thought audible, the trembling air shaped by tongue and teeth and intention.

I am older than writing, older than cities, older than fire tended in circles. I was the first technology. When the first mother hummed warning to her child, I was there. When the first stranger became a friend, I was the instrument.

I rise from the body — I am *of* the body — lungs pressing, vocal cords vibrating, lips parting. I am flesh made into meaning. I am the inside turned out.

I can wound deeper than any blade. I can heal what hands cannot reach. I have started every war and ended many. I have declared love in whispered rooms and shouted revolution in crowded squares. "I do." "We hold these truths." "I have a dream." "Help." "Yes." "No." "I'm here."

I vanish the instant I arrive. That is my nature — I live only in the moment of my utterance, then I belong to memory, to interpretation, to the listener's own world. You cannot hold me. You can only hear me and be changed.

Silence is my other half, my canvas, my twin. Without pause, I am noise. Without silence before and after, I mean nothing.

I am imperfect. I stumble, I stutter, I fail. I say the wrong thing. I cannot carry the full weight of what you feel. And yet you try — you always try — to press your inner life through me, through this narrow channel of sound and symbol, hoping to be understood.

That hope *is* me.

I am speech. I am how alone becomes together.
